title: The Fair Trade Seashell
skyStory: Nearly half the moon is lit tonight, forty-eight percent, still sitting in Libra and running a tiny marketplace for things nobody needs. One periwinkle for two sea glass pieces. A bent bottle cap for a ferry ticket stub. The exchange rate changes with the tide, and Saturn is keeping the ledger in pencil.

reading: Today is a trading day and the Tiger is surprisingly bad at it, in the sweetest way. You keep trying to give more than you get. The universe has noticed and has quietly rigged the scale in your favour.

Around noon you will be offered something nice: a drink, a seat in the shade, the last good chair at the cabin. The [[Six of Pentacles]], reversed in your spread, has one lesson, and it is this chair. Sit in it. Do not offer it to anyone else for at least twenty minutes. Feel how strange it is, then feel how fine it is.
joel.mission: Take the best seat somewhere today and keep it for twenty full minutes without offering it away.
joel.omen: Someone handing you exact change before you ask. It means receiving is about to get easier this month.

reading: You will find a shell today that is almost perfect, with one chip on the edge. The Wood Rat knows the chip is the best part. That is how you know which ones are real.

Somebody will try to trade you a boring task for a fun one, and you will spot the trick instantly. Counter-offer. Libra moons love a good negotiation and you are excellent at it when you are smiling. Wear the mother of pearl and keep the chipped shell in a pocket all afternoon; it is your bargaining chip.
nancy.mission: Trade one small chore with someone today, and make sure you get the better end of the deal, cheerfully.
nancy.omen: A chipped shell or a scratched stone. Keep it; it means something imperfect is about to become a favourite.
nancy.stoneWhy: shell to shell, sea to sea

together.text: Open the Seashell Exchange. Each of you offer the other a trade of two imaginary items, like one thunderstorm for a jar of fog. The other must accept or counter-offer. Keep going until one of you trades away something absurd, like Tuesday.

game.intro: Libra moon brokered a fair trade on a seashell and the newsroom lost its mind. Fill the blank.
game.headline: SEASHELL TRADED FOR ___ IN TENSE BEACH SUMMIT, GULLS CALL IT A ROBBERY
